Joyce Kilmer Park.text: Named for the poet who wrote 'Trees'. You came in from the street, which is how a park becomes a place you can aim for.

1520 Sedgwick Avenue.text: The apartment building where hip hop was born in 1973. The skyline photo skips the street you just used.

Lorelei Fountain.text: A fountain honoring poet Heinrich Heine, rejected by Düsseldorf. That detail lives on the block, not in a directions app.

Bronx General Post Office.text: Its lobby has murals painted by Ben Shahn and Bernarda Bryson. Standing here is how the name becomes a place you can find again.

Loew's Paradise Theater.text: A 1929 movie palace with a ceiling painted like a starry sky. That detail lives on the block, not in a directions app.

St. George Terminal.text: The Staten Island Ferry is free and runs 24 hours a day. A search result cannot show you which way the door faces the street.

Staten Island Borough Hall.text: Its clock tower greets every ferry arriving from Manhattan. That detail lives on the block, not in a directions app.

Postcards.text: Staten Island's 9/11 memorial, shaped like two folded postcards. A search result cannot show you which way the door faces the street.

Snug Harbor Cultural Center.text: Built in 1833 as a home for retired sailors. The route you just took is the part a map usually erases.

Wagner College.text: Its hilltop campus looks out over New York Harbor. You can point to it from the corner now. That is a mental map, not a bookmark.

Silver Lake Park.text: Its lake is really a reservoir for the island's water. You can point to it from the corner now. That is a mental map, not a bookmark.

Tompkinsville Park.text: Near the spot where Henry Hudson's crew got fresh water in 1609. You can point to it from the corner now. That is a mental map, not a bookmark.

Fort Wadsworth.text: One of the oldest military sites in the country, guarding the Narrows. That detail lives on the block, not in a directions app.

Enoteca Maria.text: Its chefs are grandmothers from around the world, cooking in rotation. The line out front is part of the map. An app will not show you that.

National Lighthouse Museum.text: On the site of the old US Lighthouse Service depot. You will remember the corner, not the search result.

Staten Island Museum.text: Founded in 1881, it has art, science, and history under one roof. You will remember the corner, not the search result.

Alice Austen House.text: Home of Alice Austen, one of America's first female photographers. The building's place in the grid is the part a ticket page skips.

Staten Island Children's Museum.text: A hands-on museum inside the grounds of Snug Harbor. You will remember the corner, not the search result.

Garibaldi-Meucci Museum.text: Home of Antonio Meucci, an early telephone inventor. Getting here on foot is how this stop becomes part of your own map.

Staten Island Zoo.text: Famous for its large reptile collection and its groundhog, Chuck. You did not teleport to the lawn. You arrived, and that is the lesson.

Clove Lakes Park.text: Home to the oldest living thing in NYC, a 300-year-old tulip tree. Standing in it is how you learn what the blocks beside it feel like.

Von Briesen Park.text: A cliff-top park with a close view of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge. You came in from the street, which is how a park becomes a place you can aim for.

Richmond County Bank Ballpark.text: A ballpark with the Manhattan skyline behind the outfield. Standing here is how the name becomes a place you can find again.

St. George Theatre.text: A 1929 movie palace with a Spanish-Baroque interior. Arriving on foot is what makes the next block familiar.

ferry.text: This boat is the fast way to Staten Island. It is public transit, and the hunters cannot board.
